purpose: A small set of explicitly labeled measures that illuminate the mechanism without pooling unlike populations.

measures.comparison: The same survey reports 15% in the comparable 2019 survey.
measures.interpretation: Care is present inside working life; this is not proof of a cross-country trend.

measures.comparison: The report also estimates 6% of UK adults gave up work to care.
measures.interpretation: Care pressure can convert into labor-market exit; the estimate is survey-reported and population-specific.

measures.unit: percent of eligible carers in England
measures.comparison: This denominator is eligible carers known to English councils, not all UK adults or workers.
measures.interpretation: A similar mechanism appears in a different administrative population, but the percentages are not directly comparable.

measures.comparison: High-intensity care is measured within the English carer population.
measures.interpretation: Time intensity is a plausible route from care demand to work, health, and household-room constraints.

measures.unit: percent of carers on a diary day
measures.comparison: Non-carers’ corresponding diary-day participation was 7.0%; this is a within-country time-use contrast, not a prevalence estimate.
measures.interpretation: Care consumes observed daily time and is a distinct route from employment or service outcomes.

measures.unit: percent of carers receiving local-authority support or services
measures.comparison: Support satisfaction is observed only among carers who received local-authority support or services.
measures.interpretation: Care need does not automatically convert into usable or satisfying support.

next_test: Acquire harmonized UK/England/Australia measures with stable population definitions and repeated periods, then test direction and effect size without treating survey, administrative, and diary denominators as interchangeable.
boundary: These measures describe related mechanisms but are not a pooled prevalence, causal estimate, market size, or company-impact estimate.
